page.layout: Two columns of one printed page, separated by a vertical rule. Left column: entries from Hiph. through Rad. ש. Right column: entries from relinquentur through & se-. Running head ש at the top of each column. Page number 193 at top right. Catchword "dere" and signature "B b" at the foot.

main_text.p: concatenabitur, fut. Niph. 3. f. m. R. רָתַק
שׁ, vel יֵשׁ est, יְשָׁךְ tu es, יִשְׁנוֹ ille est, יֵשְׁכֶם vos estis, &c. est part. indeclin. aff. in Rad. יֶשׁ.

יִשָּׂא feret, יִשְׂאֵךְ te, יִשְׂאֻהוּ eum, יִשְׂאֶנָּה eam, וַיִּשָּׂאֵם & tulit eos, יִשְׂאוּם ferent eos, יִשְׂאוּ ferent eum, יִשְּׂאֻנוּ ferent nos, & יִשְּׂאֻךָ ferent te, &c. fut. Kal, 3. f. & pl. m. aff. R. נָשָׂא.
יִשָּׂאוּ ferent, pro יִשָּׂא, fut. Kal, 3. pl. m. R. נָשָׂא.
יִשָּׁא, vel יִשִּׁיא decipiet, יִשָּׁאוּ, vel יִשִּׁיאוּ decipient, fut. Hiph. 3. f. & pl. m. R. נָשָׂא.
יִשָּׁאוּן tumultuabuntur, fut. Niph. 3. pl. m. parag. Rad. שָׁאָה.
יִשָּׁאֵר relinquetur; יִשְׁאֲרוּ relinquent, fut. Niph. & Hiph. 3. f. & pl. m. Rad. שָׁאַר.
quent, fut. Niph. & Hiph. 3. f. & pl. m. Rad. שָׁאַר.
וַיִּשְׁבֶּה et captivum abduxit, וַיִּשְׁבּוּ & captivos abduxerunt, fut. Kal, 3. f. m. apoc. (pro יִשְׁבָּה) & 3. pl. m. Rad. שָׁבָה.
וַיָּשָׁב, וַיָּשֶׁב & redire fecit, fut. Hiph. 3. f. m. Rad. שׁוּב.
יָשַׁב sedebit, יֵשְׁבוּ sedebunt, fut. Kal, 3. f. & pl. m. Rad. יָשַׁב.
יָשַׁב sedere, Infin. Kal, Rad. יָשַׁב.
וְהַיּשֵׁב & qui sederit, הַיּשֵׁבִי qui residens es, הַיּשִׁבָה quae residet, יֹשְׁבֵיהֶם habitatores eorum, part. Ben. Kal, f. m. parag. & sing. fæm. ut & pl. m. aff. Rad. יָשַׁב.

page.notes: Hebrew words were read from a low-resolution scan. The vowel points and final letters are my best reading and should be checked against the original before use. The Hebrew in the entry headings and the right-hand verb forms is especially uncertain. Printed page number 193 is read from the top right corner. The running head is the Hebrew letter Shin repeated on both columns. Column breaks are marked by the hyphens "re-/linquet" and "relin-/quent" and by the catchword "dere".
